title: USC OIS: On-Campus Employment (curated summary)
text:
USC OIS says F-1 undergraduate and graduate students may start eligible on-campus employment in their first semester. The university lists a 20-hour weekly limit during fall and spring and up to 40 hours during summer and official university breaks. Add together hours from all campus jobs when checking the limit.
USC on-campus work and enrollment: payroll's student-employment unit thresholds differ from immigration's full-time enrollment requirements. Holding a campus job does not itself permit dropping below the F-1 study requirement; OIS must approve an applicable exception. The page describes special treatment for final-semester students and certain thesis, dissertation, or qualifying-exam registrations.
USC campus job search: use the Career Center and university job resources. International students do not qualify for federally funded Work-Study positions. Off-campus employment needs its own appropriate authorization; do not assume a job is authorized merely because it is associated with USC. Confirm ambiguous campus/employer arrangements with OIS.
curation_note: Concise paraphrase checked against the linked USC page via web retrieval. Not a complete page snapshot or a substitute for OIS advice.
